claude.performance_metric: product shut down ~66 months (April 9, 2015) after close; team integration succeeded
claude.rationale: gap_45=1: the FriendFeed.com product (T4) crossed into Facebook ownership but was kept "for the time being" in maintenance/read-only while the engineering processes (T5) integrated into Facebook's own teams rather than continuing to produce/deliver the FriendFeed product — a structural product-vs-process mismatch at closing (§2 T4, T5). gap_56=0: the operational engineering capability (T5) and the people/organization (T6) transferred together — "all FriendFeed employees will join Facebook," founders in senior roles (§2 T5, T6). p4_pathway=0 and p5_pathway=0: §4 documents no product-process disruption (product decline/shutdown was a deliberate wind-down, not a fracture) and no process-organization fracture (people and engineering roles moved together). Gap in B was not documented as contractually absorbed via any transitional-services agreement (§5), so gap_mitigated=no.

gemini.rationale: The deal was an acqui-hire where the engineering team and processes (T5, T6) transferred into Facebook, but the FriendFeed product (T4) was effectively abandoned/wound down, creating a structural gap at closing (gap_45=1). However, this was intentional, so no P4 disruption pathway manifested. T5 and T6 moved together seamlessly (gap_56=0, p5_pathway=0).

grok.rationale: gap_45=1 from T2/T4 lines (standalone model terminated; product kept read-only then wound down) while T5/T6 transferred intact. gap_56=0 from T5/T6 lines (engineering capability and all employees moved together). p4_pathway=0 and p5_pathway=0 per section 4 (explicitly none documented; wind-down was deliberate, not fracture).
